symbols.name: Libtmux
nativeDocumentation:
Native captured values, typed queries and explicit command descriptions.

    A {!Snapshot.t} owns immutable observations. Entity accessors and query
    evaluation perform no I/O, preserve captured order and remain usable after
    client closure. Use [Libtmux_unix.Client] or [Libtmux_eio.Client] to acquire
    or mutate state.

    Retaining any entity retains its complete snapshot graph. Copy scalar
    summaries when captured relationships are no longer needed. Targets omit the
    graph but remain restricted to their original {!Source.t}.

    {1 Typical flow}

    Capture explicitly, traverse {!Session.window_links} and {!Window.panes},
    filter with [Seq.filter] or {!Query.matching}, establish cardinality with
    {!Query.exactly_one}, then submit a command with a bound target.

    The core depends only on the standard library. Its abstract observations are
    safe to share; live clients and subscriptions belong to their backend.

    See the
    {{:https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/graph.md}graph
     guide} for window links and the
    {{:https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/queries.md}query
     guide} for native predicates and typed expressions.

doc.summary: Native captured values, typed queries and explicit command descriptions.

A {!Snapshot.t} owns immutable observations. Entity accessors and query evaluation perform no I/O, preserve captured order and remain usable after client closure. Use `Libtmux_unix.Client` or `Libtmux_eio.Client` to acquire or mutate state.

Retaining any entity retains its complete snapshot graph. Copy scalar summaries when captured relationships are no longer needed. Targets omit the graph but remain restricted to their original {!Source.t}.

## Typical flow

Capture explicitly, traverse {!Session.window_links} and {!Window.panes}, filter with `Seq.filter` or {!Query.matching}, establish cardinality with {!Query.exactly_one}, then submit a command with a bound target.

The core depends only on the standard library. Its abstract observations are safe to share; live clients and subscriptions belong to their backend.

See the [graph guide](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/graph.md) for window links and the [query guide](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/queries.md) for native predicates and typed expressions.

An explicit socket description. Constructing an endpoint neither reads the
    environment nor starts a daemon. {!Source.t} adds the observed daemon and

declarations.text:
module Endpoint : sig
  type t
  (** An explicit socket description, independent of the environment. *)

  type kind = Named_socket of string | Socket_path of string

  val named_socket : string -> t
  (** [named_socket name] describes tmux's [-L name] endpoint. Raises
      [Invalid_argument] if [name] is empty or contains NUL or [/]. *)

  val socket_path : string -> t
  (** [socket_path path] describes an absolute [-S path] endpoint. It does not
      check existence or resolve symbolic links. Raises [Invalid_argument] if
      [path] is relative, empty or contains NUL. *)

  val kind : t -> kind

  val equal : t -> t -> bool
  (** Equality compares descriptions, not server instances or resolved paths. *)

  val pp : Format.formatter -> t -> unit
end

symbols.name: Expr
nativeDocumentation:
Inspectable predicates whose entity and operand types are checked by the
    compiler. Combine native closures separately with [Seq.filter]. Evaluation
    follows captured relationships without acquisition or hidden caches.

declarations.text:
module Expr : sig
  type 'entity t

  val all : 'a t list -> 'a t
  (** Boolean conjunction; the empty conjunction is true. *)

  val any : 'a t list -> 'a t
  (** Boolean disjunction; the empty disjunction is false. *)

  val not_ : 'a t -> 'a t

  module Bool : sig
    val equal : ('a, bool) Field.t -> bool -> 'a t
    val is_true : ('a, bool) Field.t -> 'a t
    val is_false : ('a, bool) Field.t -> 'a t
  end

  module Int : sig
    val equal : ('a, int) Field.t -> int -> 'a t
    val lt : ('a, int) Field.t -> int -> 'a t
    val le : ('a, int) Field.t -> int -> 'a t
    val gt : ('a, int) Field.t -> int -> 'a t
    val ge : ('a, int) Field.t -> int -> 'a t
    val is_in : ('a, int) Field.t -> int list -> 'a t
  end

  module Text : sig
    val equal : ('a, string) Field.t -> string -> 'a t
    val starts_with : ('a, string) Field.t -> string -> 'a t
    val ends_with : ('a, string) Field.t -> string -> 'a t
    val contains : ('a, string) Field.t -> string -> 'a t

    val is_in : ('a, string) Field.t -> string list -> 'a t
    (** Comparisons use exact bytes, without case folding or normalization. The
        empty substring matches every string. *)
  end

  module Rel : sig
    val any : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t -> 'b t -> 'a t
    val all : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t -> 'b t -> 'a t

    val none : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t -> 'b t -> 'a t
    (** On empty relations, [any] is false; [all] and [none] are true. One child
        must satisfy the complete nested expression. *)

    val is : ('a, 'b) Relation.One.t -> 'b t -> 'a t
    val exists : ('a, 'b) Relation.Optional.t -> 'b t -> 'a t
    val is_absent : ('a, 'b) Relation.Optional.t -> 'a t
  end

  val compile : 'a t -> 'a -> bool
  (** Prepare a reusable predicate. Compilation and evaluation perform no I/O.
  *)

  val pp : Format.formatter -> 'a t -> unit
  val describe : 'a t -> string

  type _ comparison =
    | Bool_equal : bool -> bool comparison
    | Int_equal : int -> int comparison
    | Int_lt : int -> int comparison
    | Int_le : int -> int comparison
    | Int_gt : int -> int comparison
    | Int_ge : int -> int comparison
    | Int_in : int list -> int comparison
    | Text_equal : string -> string comparison
    | Text_starts_with : string -> string comparison
    | Text_ends_with : string -> string comparison
    | Text_contains : string -> string comparison
    | Text_in : string list -> string comparison

  type 'a view =
    | Compare : ('a, 'v) Field.t * 'v comparison -> 'a view
    | All of 'a t list
    | Any of 'a t list
    | Not of 'a t
    | Related_any : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t * 'b t -> 'a view
    | Related_all : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t * 'b t -> 'a view
    | Related_none : ('a, 'b) Relation.Many.t * 'b t -> 'a view
    | Related_one : ('a, 'b) Relation.One.t * 'b t -> 'a view
    | Related_optional : ('a, 'b) Relation.Optional.t * 'b t -> 'a view
    | Absent : ('a, 'b) Relation.Optional.t -> 'a view

  val view : 'a t -> 'a view
  (** Typed read-only inspection for codecs and planners. A view cannot add
      custom accessors or closures to an expression. *)
end

doc.summary: Inspectable predicates whose entity and operand types are checked by the compiler. Combine native closures separately with `Seq.filter`. Evaluation follows captured relationships without acquisition or hidden caches.

declarations.text:
module Formats : sig
  module Kind : sig
    type t = Text | Timestamp
  end

  module Context : sig
    type t =
      | Server
      | Connection
      | Session
      | Window
      | Window_link
      | Pane
      | Client
      | Buffer
      | Mouse
      | Command
  end

  type descriptor = {
    name : string;
    kind : Kind.t;
    contexts : Context.t list;
    versions : string list;
  }
  (** Metadata generated from pinned tmux format callbacks. [contexts] lists
      direct context dependencies, not a promise that a value exists. Caller
      variables from hooks and menus are outside this built-in catalog. *)

  type observation =
    | Snapshot of Snapshot.t
    | Session of Session.t
    | Window of Window.t
    | Window_link of Window_link.t
    | Pane of Pane.t
    | Client of Client_observation.t

  type scalar = Bool of bool | Int of int | Text of string

  type state =
    | Value of scalar
    | Missing
    | Unacquired
    | Unsupported
        (** [Missing] is an absence explicitly recorded in the observation, such
            as a client without terminal height. [Unacquired] means no captured
            value for this observation, including ambiguous session context for
            a pane. [Unsupported] means the name is outside the selected
            release's catalog. [Value (Text "")] is a captured empty string,
            never inferred absence. *)

  val catalog : version:string -> (descriptor Iarray.t, Error.t) result
  val describe : version:string -> string -> (descriptor option, Error.t) result

  val lookup :
    version:string -> observation -> string -> (state, Error.t) result
  (** No I/O. Supply the version recorded by the acquiring client's [version]
      accessor. Unsupported catalog versions return an error. Native typed
      accessors remain the primary API; lookup does not acquire extra fields. *)
end

module Context : sig
    type t =
      | Server
      | Connection

symbols.name: Operations
nativeDocumentation:
Construct typed tmux operations for a backend client. Observations are
    immutable, mutations use explicit targets, and no command retries a mutation
    against another connection generation. Construction performs no I/O; the
    descriptions below state what execution does.

declarations.text:
module Operations : sig
  val capture : unit -> Snapshot.t Command.t
  (** Capture and validate the complete session/window-link/pane graph. The
      result records an acquisition interval, not an atomic server instant. *)

  val capture_text :
    ?scratch_dir:string ->
    Pane.t ->
    start:int ->
    end_:int ->
    Captured_text.t Command.t
  (** Capture inclusive visible rows through an operation-owned temporary file.
      Require [0 <= start <= end_ < Pane.height pane]; scrollback is excluded.
      Retained bytes survive client close. The scratch directory must share the
      daemon filesystem. *)

  val rename_window : Window.target -> name:string -> unit Command.t
  (** Set the global window name. Every session link observes the new name on
      its next capture; existing snapshots retain the old value. *)

  val rename_session : Session.target -> name:string -> unit Command.t
  (** Set the session name, rejecting a conflicting existing name. Bound IDs
      remain usable; existing snapshots retain their captured names. *)

  val switch_client_at :
    ?update_environment:bool ->
    Client_name.t ->
    session:Session.target ->
    unit Command.t
  (** Switch the client currently bearing this name to the bound session.
      Environment updates are disabled by default. This can move either a
      terminal client or a control client; it does not open a new terminal. *)

  val request_detach_client_at : Client_name.t -> unit Command.t
  (** Request detachment of the client currently bearing this name. Success
      confirms request processing, not peer exit. Detaching the library's own
      primary lane can lose the response and retire its generation. *)

  val refresh_client_at : ?status_only:bool -> Client_name.t -> unit Command.t
  (** Request a redraw; no terminal-rendering completion is implied. *)

  val resize_control_client_at :
    Client_name.t -> width:int -> height:int -> unit Command.t
  (** Set a control client's reported size. tmux rejects terminal clients. *)

  val send_text : Pane.target -> text:string -> unit Command.t
  (** Literal bytes, without an implicit Enter. NUL is rejected at admission. *)

  val send_keys : Pane.target -> Key.t list -> unit Command.t
  (** Send named tmux keys in order, without an implicit Enter. Use {!send_text}
      for literal bytes rather than key interpretation. *)

  val wait_for : string -> unit Command.t
  (** Wait on a named tmux semaphore using a dedicated bound lane. *)

  val signal : string -> unit Command.t
  (** Signal a named tmux semaphore, releasing a waiter or retaining the signal
      for a later {!wait_for}. This does not signal an OS process. *)

  val capture_environment :
    ?hidden:bool -> Environment.scope -> Environment.t Command.t
  (** Acquire a bounded table through a read-only command process. Its response
      must identify the bound daemon while the original pidfd remains live.
      Unsupported external variable names fail decoding; they are not omitted.
  *)

  val set_environment :
    ?hidden:bool -> Environment.scope -> name:string -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Set a local environment value for future pane processes. [hidden] defaults
      to false; hidden values remain internal to tmux. Existing processes keep
      their environment. *)

  val unset_environment : Environment.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Remove the local entry, allowing a global value to apply to future panes.
  *)

  val remove_environment : Environment.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Store a removal marker, excluding the variable from future panes. *)

  val capture_options :
    ?include_inherited:bool -> Options.scope -> Options.t Command.t
  (** Acquire one bounded option table, excluding hooks. The default includes
      only local entries. Inherited table enumeration includes built-ins;
      inherited user options require [read_option] with their explicit name.
      Built-in descriptors cover every supported release from tmux 3.3a through
      3.8; other versions return {!Error.Unsupported}. *)

  val read_option :
    ?include_inherited:bool ->
    Options.scope ->
    string ->
    Options.value option Command.t
  (** Read one exact name, including user-option inheritance. [None] means no
      entry under the selected policy. An invalid target remains an error. The
      default follows inheritance; this does not identify the defining parent
      scope. *)

  val set_option :
    ?index:int ->
    ?append:bool ->
    Options.scope ->
    name:string ->
    Options.scalar ->
    unit Command.t
  (** Validate the scope and scalar kind before admission. Array values require
      an index, or [append:true]. Without an index, tmux splits appended text
      using the option's separator and fills the lowest unused indexes. Text is
      literal; tmux format expansion is disabled. Hooks use a separate
      operation. *)

  val unset_option : ?index:int -> Options.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Remove a local override or one array element. Global built-ins reset to
      their tmux defaults; this does not recursively unset child overrides. *)

  val clear_option_array : Options.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Set a local empty array, masking inheritance. *)

  val capture_hooks : Options.scope -> Options.t Command.t
  (** Capture locally configured built-in hooks. Command values are tmux's
      printed representation, retained as data. *)

  val read_hook :
    ?include_inherited:bool ->
    Options.scope ->
    string ->
    Options.value option Command.t
  (** Read an exact hook name. Inheritance is included by default; [None] means
      no entry under the selected policy. Missing targets remain errors. *)

  val set_hook :
    ?index:int ->
    ?append:bool ->
    Options.scope ->
    name:string ->
    Hook.command list ->
    unit Command.t
  (** Set a hook to a nonempty command list. Without an index, replace the whole
      hook array, or fill the lowest free index when appending. An explicit
      [@name] custom hook stores command text as a user option; it requires
      complete replacement and has no array indexes. [read_hook] returns its
      [Options.Text] value; bulk hook capture includes built-ins. Commands may
      cause arbitrary tmux effects when triggered. Hooks that print output are
      outside the supported control transport contract. *)

  val remove_hook : ?index:int -> Options.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Remove the local hook or one indexed array entry. An inherited hook may
      become effective again; this does not stop work it already started. *)

  val run_hook : Options.scope -> string -> unit Command.t
  (** Run the effective hook in an explicit session, window or pane context. A
      successful result follows completion of its synchronous command queue.
      Background work started by a hook has its own lifetime. A later hook
      failure returns an uncertain outcome; preceding effects remain. Named [@]
      hooks return [Unsupported] because tmux can hide their parse failures in
      the server log. Configuration and inspection remain available. *)

  val create_session :
    ?window_name:string ->
    ?width:int ->
    ?height:int ->
    ?spawn:Spawn.t ->
    name:string ->
    unit ->
    Created.t Command.t
  (** Create a detached session on the bound daemon. Name collisions fail. *)

  val create_window :
    ?index:int ->
    ?name:string ->
    ?spawn:Spawn.t ->
    Session.target ->
    Created.t Command.t
  (** Create detached, rejecting an occupied explicit index. *)

  val split_pane :
    ?size:Geometry.size ->
    ?spawn:Spawn.t ->
    Pane.target ->
    direction:Geometry.direction ->
    Created.t Command.t
  (** Create a detached pane beside the target and return the IDs reported by
      tmux. Omitted [size] lets tmux choose the split; tmux rejects splits when
      no space remains. *)

  val break_pane :
    ?name:string ->
    Pane.target ->
    session:Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    Created.t Command.t
  (** Move the pane into a new window at an explicit session index. An occupied
      destination fails. The returned IDs describe the resulting context; the
      pane itself already existed. *)

  val kill_session : Session.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Remove the session and its window links. Windows with no other links and
      their panes are destroyed. Removing the last session may stop tmux. *)

  val kill_window : Window.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Destroy the window, all its session links and every contained pane. This
      acts on the global window, not a single contextual link. *)

  val kill_pane : Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Destroy the target pane and its running process. tmux removes a window
      that becomes empty and may remove its now-empty sessions. *)

  val select_window_at : Session.target -> index:int -> unit Command.t
  (** Operate on the session's current index at execution, not an old link
      incarnation. *)

  val unlink_window_at :
    ?allow_kill:bool -> Session.target -> index:int -> unit Command.t
  (** Without [allow_kill], tmux rejects removal of the last link to a window.
  *)

  val link_window :
    Window.target -> session:Session.target -> index:int -> unit Command.t
  (** Add a session-specific link to the global window at [index], rejecting an
      occupied index. The source window and its panes stay shared. *)

  val move_window_at :
    Session.target ->
    from_index:int ->
    session:Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    unit Command.t
  (** Move the source session's current link at [from_index]. Destination
      collisions fail. *)

  val select_pane : Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Make the pane active in its containing window. This does not open or
      attach a terminal client. *)

  val set_pane_title : Pane.target -> title:string -> unit Command.t
  (** Set the pane title as literal text, without tmux format expansion. A
      running terminal application can subsequently replace the title. *)

  val resize_pane : ?width:int -> ?height:int -> Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Request positive cell dimensions, supplying at least one dimension. Omit
      either dimension to retain it. tmux can constrain the result to the
      available layout. Capture again to observe the actual dimensions. *)

  val resize_window :
    ?width:int -> ?height:int -> Window.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Request positive cell dimensions, supplying at least one dimension. Omit
      either dimension to retain it. Client-size and window-size policies can
      affect subsequent sizing. *)

  val select_layout : Window.target -> Layout.t -> unit Command.t
  (** Apply a preset or validated custom layout to the window. Pane geometry
      follows tmux layout rules; capture again to observe the result. *)

  val cycle_layout : Window.target -> [ `Next | `Previous ] -> unit Command.t
  (** Select the next or previous tmux preset layout for this window. *)

  val move_pane :
    ?size:Geometry.size ->
    Pane.target ->
    beside:Pane.target ->
    direction:Geometry.direction ->
    unit Command.t
  (** Move the source pane beside another pane, optionally setting the split
      size. Both targets must belong to the same bound generation. An emptied
      source window is removed by tmux. *)

  val swap_panes : Pane.target -> Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Exchange pane positions without exchanging their identities or running
      processes. Both targets must belong to the same bound generation. *)

  val rotate_panes : Window.target -> [ `Forward | `Backward ] -> unit Command.t
  (** Rotate pane positions in the selected direction. Pane identities and
      running processes remain attached to their panes. *)

  val zoom_pane : Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Toggle the window's zoom state around this pane. *)

  val respawn_pane :
    ?kill_running:bool -> Pane.target -> Spawn.t -> unit Command.t
  (** Start the supplied command in the existing pane. A running process causes
      failure unless [kill_running:true] explicitly replaces it. The pane ID
      remains unchanged. *)

  val clear_history : Pane.target -> unit Command.t
  (** Clear stored scrollback for this pane. The visible screen and running
      process remain; later captures cannot recover discarded history. *)
end

symbols.name: Output
nativeDocumentation:
Future observed pane bytes, local cursors and explicit continuity loss.
    Output cursors are unrelated to snapshot times or server-side history.

declarations.text:
module Output : sig
  type cursor = { generation : Generation.t; offset : int64 }
  (** [offset] is the number of observed bytes through the end of a Data event.
      Cursors from different subscription generations are unrelated. No cursor
      identifies a snapshot instant or a server-side historical position. *)

  type reason =
    | Overflow
    | Membership_changed
    | Server_paused
    | Cancelled
    | Client_closed
    | Transport_error of Error.t

  type event =
    | Data of { cursor : cursor; bytes : string }
    | Gap of { after : cursor option; lost_bytes : int option; reason : reason }
    | End of reason
        (** Immutable event values. [Gap.after] is the last cursor delivered to
            the caller. Unknown loss is [None]. A gap ends continuity and is
            followed by End; recover with a fresh capture and a new
            subscription. Data preserves bytes, including NUL and invalid UTF-8.
            It is future observed output, not rendered text or historical
            reconstruction. *)

  val reason_pp : Format.formatter -> reason -> unit

  type wait_error =
    | Ended of reason
    | Failure of Error.t
        (** A future-byte wait either loses its subscription's continuity or
            fails an operation. Neither result establishes that the text was
            absent earlier. *)
end

doc.summary: Future observed pane bytes, local cursors and explicit continuity loss. Output cursors are unrelated to snapshot times or server-side history.

  (** [matching expression] compiles once when the adapter is constructed.

open Libtmux
module Client = Libtmux_unix.Client
module Workspace = Libtmux_unix.Workspace
module Config = Libtmux_workspace.Config
module Plan = Libtmux_workspace.Plan
module Execution = Libtmux_workspace.Execution

let get = function
  | Ok value -> value
  | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)

let capture_graph client (initial : Created.t) spawn =
  let linked =
    get
      (Client.create_session client ~name:"linked" ~window_name:"linked-home"
         ~spawn ())
  in
  let pane =
    Snapshot.find_pane
      (get (Client.capture client))
      (Pane.Target.id linked.pane)
    |> Option.get
  in
  let text = "showcase ready" in
  ignore (get (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane ~text));
  get
    (Client.link_window client initial.window ~session:linked.session ~index:7);
  get (Client.capture client)

let print_graph snapshot =
  Snapshot.sessions snapshot
  |> Iarray.iter (fun session ->
      Session.window_links session
      |> Iarray.iter (fun link ->
          let window = Window_link.window link in
          Printf.printf "%s/%d %s: %d pane(s)\n" (Session.name session)
            (Window_link.index link) (Window.name window)
            (Iarray.length (Window.panes window))));
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.sessions snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.windows snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.window_links snapshot) = 3);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.panes snapshot) = 2);
  print_endline "graph: 2 sessions, 2 windows, 3 links, 2 panes"

let with_demo binary use =
  let directory = Filename.temp_dir "libtmux-ocaml-showcase-" "" in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Sys.readdir directory
      |> Array.iter (fun name -> Sys.remove (Filename.concat directory name));
      Unix.rmdir directory)
    (fun () ->
      let socket = Filename.concat directory "server" in
      (* Give this private daemon a lifetime even if startup fails. *)
      let config_file = Filename.concat directory "tmux.conf" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text config_file (fun output ->
          output_string output "set-option -s exit-unattached on\n");
      let wrapper = Filename.concat directory "tmux" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text wrapper (fun output ->
          Printf.fprintf output "#!/bin/sh\nexec %s -f %s \"$@\"\n"
            (Filename.quote binary)
            (Filename.quote config_file));
      Unix.chmod wrapper 0o700;
      let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
      let version =
        Fun.protect
          ~finally:(fun () ->
            if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
              failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
          (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
      in
      if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
        failwith "invalid tmux version";
      let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
      let ready = Filename.concat directory "ready.txt" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text ready (fun output ->
          output_string output "showcase ready\n");
      let spawn =
        Spawn.make (Exec { program = "/bin/cat"; args = [ "-u"; ready; "-" ] })
      in
      let config =
        match
          Config.make ~directory ~session:"showcase"
            [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
      in
      let plan =
        match
          Plan.make
            ~endpoint:(Endpoint.socket_path socket)
            ~version ~observed:None config
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
      in
      let operation = get (Workspace.submit_bootstrap ~binary:wrapper plan) in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () -> get (Workspace.close operation))
        (fun () ->
          let receipt = get (Workspace.await operation) in
          if receipt.status <> Execution.Succeeded then
            failwith "workspace setup failed";
          let client = Option.get (Workspace.client operation) in
          let initial = List.hd (Iarray.get receipt.steps 0).created in
          Printf.printf "socket=%s\n%!" socket;
          let pane =
            Snapshot.find_pane
              (get (Client.capture client))
              (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
            |> Option.get
          in
          ignore
            (get
               (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane
                  ~text:"showcase ready"));
          use client initial spawn))

let () =
  let binary = if Array.length Sys.argv = 2 then Sys.argv.(1) else "tmux" in
  let snapshot = with_demo binary capture_graph in
  print_graph snapshot

nativeDocumentation:
Validate and materialize a complete captured graph without I/O. Equal
      duplicate global rows collapse in first-occurrence order; conflicting rows
      and dangling references return {!Error.Capture_raced}. Links at different
      indexes remain distinct, including within one session. At most 10,000

      Input strings are bytes; no Unicode normalization is performed.

            (Window_link.index link) (Window.name window)
            (Iarray.length (Window.panes window))));
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.sessions snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.windows snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.window_links snapshot) = 3);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.panes snapshot) = 2);
  print_endline "graph: 2 sessions, 2 windows, 3 links, 2 panes"

let with_demo binary use =
  let directory = Filename.temp_dir "libtmux-ocaml-showcase-" "" in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Sys.readdir directory
      |> Array.iter (fun name -> Sys.remove (Filename.concat directory name));
      Unix.rmdir directory)
    (fun () ->
      let socket = Filename.concat directory "server" in
      (* Give this private daemon a lifetime even if startup fails. *)
      let config_file = Filename.concat directory "tmux.conf" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text config_file (fun output ->
          output_string output "set-option -s exit-unattached on\n");
      let wrapper = Filename.concat directory "tmux" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text wrapper (fun output ->
          Printf.fprintf output "#!/bin/sh\nexec %s -f %s \"$@\"\n"
            (Filename.quote binary)
            (Filename.quote config_file));
      Unix.chmod wrapper 0o700;
      let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
      let version =
        Fun.protect
          ~finally:(fun () ->
            if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
              failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
          (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
      in
      if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
        failwith "invalid tmux version";
      let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
      let ready = Filename.concat directory "ready.txt" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text ready (fun output ->
          output_string output "showcase ready\n");
      let spawn =
        Spawn.make (Exec { program = "/bin/cat"; args = [ "-u"; ready; "-" ] })
      in
      let config =
        match
          Config.make ~directory ~session:"showcase"
            [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
      in
      let plan =
        match
          Plan.make
            ~endpoint:(Endpoint.socket_path socket)
            ~version ~observed:None config
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
      in
      let operation = get (Workspace.submit_bootstrap ~binary:wrapper plan) in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () -> get (Workspace.close operation))
        (fun () ->
          let receipt = get (Workspace.await operation) in
          if receipt.status <> Execution.Succeeded then
            failwith "workspace setup failed";
          let client = Option.get (Workspace.client operation) in
          let initial = List.hd (Iarray.get receipt.steps 0).created in
          Printf.printf "socket=%s\n%!" socket;
          let pane =
            Snapshot.find_pane
              (get (Client.capture client))
              (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
            |> Option.get
          in
          ignore
            (get
               (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane
                  ~text:"showcase ready"));
          use client initial spawn))

let () =
  let binary = if Array.length Sys.argv = 2 then Sys.argv.(1) else "tmux" in
  let snapshot = with_demo binary capture_graph in
  print_graph snapshot

symbols.name: Libtmux_eio
nativeDocumentation:
Concurrent Linux tmux clients using the application's Eio scheduler.

    Client methods perform I/O unless documented otherwise. Captured
    {!Libtmux.Snapshot} observations and retained {!Operation.inspect} remain
    local. Clients belong to the connecting domain. Closure releases their owned
    resources; tmux applies its configured daemon lifetime.

    See {!Client} for acquisition and commands, {!Operation} for cancellation
    outcomes, and {!Subscription} for bounded future output. The
    {{:https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/streaming.md}streaming
     guide} demonstrates application-owned switches, cancellation and continuity
    gaps.

symbols.name: Client
nativeDocumentation:
An explicit generation-bound connection. Applications retain ownership of
    the endpoint choice and resource lifetime.

declarations.text:
module Client : sig
  type t

  val connect :
    ?cleanup:Cleanup.t ->
    ?binary:string ->
    ?timeout:float ->
    sw:Eio.Switch.t ->
    process_mgr:_ Eio.Process.mgr ->
    mono_clock:_ Eio.Time.Mono.t ->
    Libtmux.Endpoint.t ->
    (t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Attach to an existing local Linux daemon in the same PID namespace and
      shared filesystem. Requires pidfd support. Default exchange timeout: one
      second. All client calls belong to the connecting OCaml domain. Initial
      and auxiliary attachments suppress tmux's [update-environment] behavior.
  *)

  val cleanup : t -> Cleanup.t
  (** Read the supplied report or the client's fresh default without I/O.
      {!Cleanup.inspect} remains available after close. *)

  val source : t -> Libtmux.Source.t
  (** Read the retained endpoint, daemon PID and connection generation without
      I/O. *)

  val version : t -> string
  (** Read the bound daemon's observed version without I/O. *)

  val subscribe :
    ?session:Libtmux.Session.target ->
    ?capacity_bytes:int ->
    ?capacity_events:int ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.t ->
    (Subscription.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Acquire verified coverage through one shared lane per session; choose the
      least observed session ID unless supplied. A client-owned reader delivers
      future bytes without application callbacks. Default queue bounds are 1
      MiB/1024 events; max 16 subscribers and eight total client lanes, sharing
      the 32 MiB payload budget. Queue capacities remain reserved while empty;
      captures and reads need additional scratch space and can return
      {!Libtmux.Error.Capacity} below the subscriber-count limit. See the
      {{:https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/streaming.md#plan-shared-capacity}shared
       capacity guide} for combined reservations and process slots.

      Overflow or coverage/layout changes emit Gap then End. Data starts after
      admission's marker, with no snapshot/history barrier, automatic reconnect
      or silent cursor reuse. New admission returns [Error Libtmux.Error.Closed]
      once {!close} starts. *)

  val wait_for_text :
    ?timeout:float ->
    ?scratch_dir:string ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.t ->
    text:string ->
    (Rendered.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Subscribe and capture the screen immediately, then recapture on output.
      Membership/overflow gaps establish fresh coverage in the same binding.
      Maximum pattern: 64 KiB. Return captured rendered text containing it;
      transient text may be missed. Deadlines are checked between bounded
      acquisitions, whose I/O retains the client exchange timeout. Cancellation
      propagates and releases the subscription. A cleanup failure cannot replace
      an earlier error or cancellation; inspect {!cleanup} for secondary
      failures. Otherwise cleanup failure prevents success or renewed coverage.
      No history/barrier guarantee. *)

  val submit :
    t -> 'a Libtmux.Command.t -> ('a Operation.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Validate and reserve bounded capacity without I/O. Return
      [Error Libtmux.Error.Closed] once {!close} starts. *)

  val await : 'a Operation.t -> ('a, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Cancellation propagates as Eio cancellation. Store the handle outside the
      cancelled fiber: the client drains written work independently, and the
      eventual result remains inspectable. *)

  val run : t -> 'a Libtmux.Command.t -> ('a, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Submit and await an explicit command. Retain a separate submitted handle
      when the outcome must remain inspectable after caller cancellation. *)

  val capture : t -> (Libtmux.Snapshot.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Acquire a complete immutable graph over an interval. Conflicting or
      disappearing entities fail capture; they do not become empty relations.
      The returned values remain readable after client closure. *)

  val capture_text :
    ?scratch_dir:string ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.t ->
    start:int ->
    end_:int ->
    (Rendered.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Inclusive ordinary screen rows, using a bounded private file transfer.
      Qualified local scratch storage must be shared with the daemon. *)

  (* BEGIN GENERATED OPERATIONS *)
  val rename_window :
    t -> Libtmux.Window.target -> name:string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set the global window name. Every session link observes the new name on
      its next capture; existing snapshots retain the old value. *)

  val rename_session :
    t -> Libtmux.Session.target -> name:string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set the session name, rejecting a conflicting existing name. Bound IDs
      remain usable; existing snapshots retain their captured names. *)

  val switch_client_at :
    ?update_environment:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Client_name.t ->
    session:Libtmux.Session.target ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Switch the client currently bearing this name to the bound session.
      Environment updates are disabled by default. This can move either a
      terminal client or a control client; it does not open a new terminal. *)

  val request_detach_client_at :
    t -> Libtmux.Client_name.t -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Request detachment of the client currently bearing this name. Success
      confirms request processing, not peer exit. Detaching the library's own
      primary lane can lose the response and retire its generation. *)

  val refresh_client_at :
    ?status_only:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Client_name.t ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Request a redraw; no terminal-rendering completion is implied. *)

  val resize_control_client_at :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Client_name.t ->
    width:int ->
    height:int ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set a control client's reported size. tmux rejects terminal clients. *)

  val send_text :
    t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> text:string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Literal bytes, without an implicit Enter. NUL is rejected at admission. *)

  val send_keys :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    Libtmux.Key.t list ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Send named tmux keys in order, without an implicit Enter. Use {!send_text}
      for literal bytes rather than key interpretation. *)

  val wait_for : t -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Wait on a named tmux semaphore using a dedicated bound lane. *)

  val signal : t -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Signal a named tmux semaphore, releasing a waiter or retaining the signal
      for a later {!wait_for}. This does not signal an OS process. *)

  val capture_environment :
    ?hidden:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Environment.scope ->
    (Libtmux.Environment.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Acquire a bounded table through a read-only command process. Its response
      must identify the bound daemon while the original pidfd remains live.
      Unsupported external variable names fail decoding; they are not omitted.
  *)

  val set_environment :
    ?hidden:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Environment.scope ->
    name:string ->
    string ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set a local environment value for future pane processes. [hidden] defaults
      to false; hidden values remain internal to tmux. Existing processes keep
      their environment. *)

  val unset_environment :
    t -> Libtmux.Environment.scope -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove the local entry, allowing a global value to apply to future panes.
  *)

  val remove_environment :
    t -> Libtmux.Environment.scope -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Store a removal marker, excluding the variable from future panes. *)

  val capture_options :
    ?include_inherited:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    (Libtmux.Options.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Acquire one bounded option table, excluding hooks. The default includes
      only local entries. Inherited table enumeration includes built-ins;
      inherited user options require [read_option] with their explicit name.
      Built-in descriptors cover every supported release from tmux 3.3a through
      3.8; other versions return {!Libtmux.Error.Unsupported}. *)

  val read_option :
    ?include_inherited:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    string ->
    (Libtmux.Options.value option, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Read one exact name, including user-option inheritance. [None] means no
      entry under the selected policy. An invalid target remains an error. The
      default follows inheritance; this does not identify the defining parent
      scope. *)

  val set_option :
    ?index:int ->
    ?append:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    name:string ->
    Libtmux.Options.scalar ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Validate the scope and scalar kind before admission. Array values require
      an index, or [append:true]. Without an index, tmux splits appended text
      using the option's separator and fills the lowest unused indexes. Text is
      literal; tmux format expansion is disabled. Hooks use a separate
      operation. *)

  val unset_option :
    ?index:int ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    string ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove a local override or one array element. Global built-ins reset to
      their tmux defaults; this does not recursively unset child overrides. *)

  val clear_option_array :
    t -> Libtmux.Options.scope -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set a local empty array, masking inheritance. *)

  val capture_hooks :
    t -> Libtmux.Options.scope -> (Libtmux.Options.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Capture locally configured built-in hooks. Command values are tmux's
      printed representation, retained as data. *)

  val read_hook :
    ?include_inherited:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    string ->
    (Libtmux.Options.value option, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Read an exact hook name. Inheritance is included by default; [None] means
      no entry under the selected policy. Missing targets remain errors. *)

  val set_hook :
    ?index:int ->
    ?append:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    name:string ->
    Libtmux.Hook.command list ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set a hook to a nonempty command list. Without an index, replace the whole
      hook array, or fill the lowest free index when appending. An explicit
      [@name] custom hook stores command text as a user option; it requires
      complete replacement and has no array indexes. [read_hook] returns its
      [Libtmux.Options.Text] value; bulk hook capture includes built-ins.
      Commands may cause arbitrary tmux effects when triggered. Hooks that print
      output are outside the supported control transport contract. *)

  val remove_hook :
    ?index:int ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Options.scope ->
    string ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove the local hook or one indexed array entry. An inherited hook may
      become effective again; this does not stop work it already started. *)

  val run_hook :
    t -> Libtmux.Options.scope -> string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Run the effective hook in an explicit session, window or pane context. A
      successful result follows completion of its synchronous command queue.
      Background work started by a hook has its own lifetime. A later hook
      failure returns an uncertain outcome; preceding effects remain. Named [@]
      hooks return [Unsupported] because tmux can hide their parse failures in
      the server log. Configuration and inspection remain available. *)

  val create_session :
    ?window_name:string ->
    ?width:int ->
    ?height:int ->
    ?spawn:Libtmux.Spawn.t ->
    t ->
    name:string ->
    unit ->
    (Libtmux.Created.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Create a detached session on the bound daemon. Name collisions fail. *)

  val create_window :
    ?index:int ->
    ?name:string ->
    ?spawn:Libtmux.Spawn.t ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Session.target ->
    (Libtmux.Created.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Create detached, rejecting an occupied explicit index. *)

  val split_pane :
    ?size:Libtmux.Geometry.size ->
    ?spawn:Libtmux.Spawn.t ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    direction:Libtmux.Geometry.direction ->
    (Libtmux.Created.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Create a detached pane beside the target and return the IDs reported by
      tmux. Omitted [size] lets tmux choose the split; tmux rejects splits when
      no space remains. *)

  val break_pane :
    ?name:string ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    session:Libtmux.Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    (Libtmux.Created.t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Move the pane into a new window at an explicit session index. An occupied
      destination fails. The returned IDs describe the resulting context; the
      pane itself already existed. *)

  val kill_session :
    t -> Libtmux.Session.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove the session and its window links. Windows with no other links and
      their panes are destroyed. Removing the last session may stop tmux. *)

  val kill_window : t -> Libtmux.Window.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Destroy the window, all its session links and every contained pane. This
      acts on the global window, not a single contextual link. *)

  val kill_pane : t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Destroy the target pane and its running process. tmux removes a window
      that becomes empty and may remove its now-empty sessions. *)

  val select_window_at :
    t -> Libtmux.Session.target -> index:int -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Operate on the session's current index at execution, not an old link
      incarnation. *)

  val unlink_window_at :
    ?allow_kill:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Without [allow_kill], tmux rejects removal of the last link to a window.
  *)

  val link_window :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Window.target ->
    session:Libtmux.Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Add a session-specific link to the global window at [index], rejecting an
      occupied index. The source window and its panes stay shared. *)

  val move_window_at :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Session.target ->
    from_index:int ->
    session:Libtmux.Session.target ->
    index:int ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Move the source session's current link at [from_index]. Destination
      collisions fail. *)

  val select_pane : t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Make the pane active in its containing window. This does not open or
      attach a terminal client. *)

  val set_pane_title :
    t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> title:string -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Set the pane title as literal text, without tmux format expansion. A
      running terminal application can subsequently replace the title. *)

  val resize_pane :
    ?width:int ->
    ?height:int ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Request positive cell dimensions, supplying at least one dimension. Omit
      either dimension to retain it. tmux can constrain the result to the
      available layout. Capture again to observe the actual dimensions. *)

  val resize_window :
    ?width:int ->
    ?height:int ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Window.target ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Request positive cell dimensions, supplying at least one dimension. Omit
      either dimension to retain it. Client-size and window-size policies can
      affect subsequent sizing. *)

  val select_layout :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Window.target ->
    Libtmux.Layout.t ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Apply a preset or validated custom layout to the window. Pane geometry
      follows tmux layout rules; capture again to observe the result. *)

  val cycle_layout :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Window.target ->
    [ `Next | `Previous ] ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Select the next or previous tmux preset layout for this window. *)

  val move_pane :
    ?size:Libtmux.Geometry.size ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    beside:Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    direction:Libtmux.Geometry.direction ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Move the source pane beside another pane, optionally setting the split
      size. Both targets must belong to the same bound generation. An emptied
      source window is removed by tmux. *)

  val swap_panes :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Exchange pane positions without exchanging their identities or running
      processes. Both targets must belong to the same bound generation. *)

  val rotate_panes :
    t ->
    Libtmux.Window.target ->
    [ `Forward | `Backward ] ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Rotate pane positions in the selected direction. Pane identities and
      running processes remain attached to their panes. *)

  val zoom_pane : t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Toggle the window's zoom state around this pane. *)

  val respawn_pane :
    ?kill_running:bool ->
    t ->
    Libtmux.Pane.target ->
    Libtmux.Spawn.t ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Start the supplied command in the existing pane. A running process causes
      failure unless [kill_running:true] explicitly replaces it. The pane ID
      remains unchanged. *)

  val clear_history : t -> Libtmux.Pane.target -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Clear stored scrollback for this pane. The visible screen and running
      process remain; later captures cannot recover discarded history. *)

  (* END GENERATED OPERATIONS *)

  val close : t -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Retire the generation and close owned control clients and descriptors.
      Reject new {!submit} and {!subscribe} calls as soon as closing starts.
      Concurrent calls await the same teardown result. Later calls retain a
      teardown failure instead of treating the closed flag as success. Each
      helper gets 200 ms of TERM grace, followed by KILL if needed and reaping.
      Other fibers can run during that wait. The grace is per helper; it does
      not bound scheduling, filesystem or uninterruptible kernel work. No signal
      targets the daemon. tmux's [exit-unattached] and [exit-empty] policies can
      end the daemon after its clients or sessions disappear. *)
end

symbols.name: close
nativeDocumentation:
Retire the generation and close owned control clients and descriptors.
      Reject new {!submit} and {!subscribe} calls as soon as closing starts.
      Concurrent calls await the same teardown result. Later calls retain a
      teardown failure instead of treating the closed flag as success. Each
      helper gets 200 ms of TERM grace, followed by KILL if needed and reaping.
      Other fibers can run during that wait. The grace is per helper; it does
      not bound scheduling, filesystem or uninterruptible kernel work. No signal
      targets the daemon. tmux's [exit-unattached] and [exit-empty] policies can
      end the daemon after its clients or sessions disappear.

nativeDocumentation:

      least observed session ID unless supplied. A client-owned reader delivers
      future bytes without application callbacks. Default queue bounds are 1
      MiB/1024 events; max 16 subscribers and eight total client lanes, sharing
      the 32 MiB payload budget. Queue capacities remain reserved while empty;
      captures and reads need additional scratch space and can return
      {!Libtmux.Error.Capacity} below the subscriber-count limit. See the
      {{:https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/streaming.md#plan-shared-capacity}shared
       capacity guide} for combined reservations and process slots.

      admission's marker, with no snapshot/history barrier, automatic reconnect
      or silent cursor reuse. New admission returns [Error Libtmux.Error.Closed]
      once {!close} starts.

open Libtmux
module Client = Libtmux_unix.Client
module Workspace = Libtmux_unix.Workspace
module Config = Libtmux_workspace.Config
module Plan = Libtmux_workspace.Plan
module Execution = Libtmux_workspace.Execution

let get = function
  | Ok value -> value
  | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)

let watch_output binary blocking (initial : Created.t) _spawn =
  Eio_main.run @@ fun env ->
  Eio.Switch.run @@ fun sw ->
  let module Client = Libtmux_eio.Client in
  let module Subscription = Libtmux_eio.Subscription in
  let client =
    get
      (Client.connect ~sw ~binary
         ~process_mgr:(Eio.Stdenv.process_mgr env)
         ~mono_clock:(Eio.Stdenv.mono_clock env)
         (Source.endpoint (Libtmux_unix.Client.source blocking)))
  in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Eio.Cancel.protect (fun () -> get (Client.close client)))
    (fun () ->
      let pane =
        Snapshot.find_pane
          (get (Client.capture client))
          (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
        |> Option.get
      in
      let subscription =
        get (Client.subscribe ~capacity_bytes:4096 client pane)
      in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () ->
          Eio.Cancel.protect (fun () -> get (Subscription.close subscription)))
        (fun () ->
          let cursor, () =
            Eio.Fiber.pair
              (fun () ->
                match
                  Subscription.wait_for_bytes ~timeout:0.5 subscription
                    ~text:"changed"
                with
                | Ok cursor -> cursor
                | Error (Output.Failure error) ->
                    failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)
                | Error (Output.Ended reason) ->
                    failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Output.reason_pp reason))
              (fun () ->
                get (Client.send_text client (Pane.target pane) ~text:"changed");
                get (Client.send_keys client (Pane.target pane) [ Key.Enter ]))
          in
          assert (cursor.offset >= 7L);
          print_endline "observed: changed"))

let with_demo binary use =
  let directory = Filename.temp_dir "libtmux-ocaml-showcase-" "" in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Sys.readdir directory
      |> Array.iter (fun name -> Sys.remove (Filename.concat directory name));
      Unix.rmdir directory)
    (fun () ->
      let socket = Filename.concat directory "server" in
      (* Give this private daemon a lifetime even if startup fails. *)
      let config_file = Filename.concat directory "tmux.conf" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text config_file (fun output ->
          output_string output "set-option -s exit-unattached on\n");
      let wrapper = Filename.concat directory "tmux" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text wrapper (fun output ->
          Printf.fprintf output "#!/bin/sh\nexec %s -f %s \"$@\"\n"
            (Filename.quote binary)
            (Filename.quote config_file));
      Unix.chmod wrapper 0o700;
      let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
      let version =
        Fun.protect
          ~finally:(fun () ->
            if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
              failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
          (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
      in
      if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
        failwith "invalid tmux version";
      let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
      let ready = Filename.concat directory "ready.txt" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text ready (fun output ->
          output_string output "showcase ready\n");
      let spawn =
        Spawn.make (Exec { program = "/bin/cat"; args = [ "-u"; ready; "-" ] })
      in
      let config =
        match
          Config.make ~directory ~session:"showcase"
            [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
      in
      let plan =
        match
          Plan.make
            ~endpoint:(Endpoint.socket_path socket)
            ~version ~observed:None config
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
      in
      let operation = get (Workspace.submit_bootstrap ~binary:wrapper plan) in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () -> get (Workspace.close operation))
        (fun () ->
          let receipt = get (Workspace.await operation) in
          if receipt.status <> Execution.Succeeded then
            failwith "workspace setup failed";
          let client = Option.get (Workspace.client operation) in
          let initial = List.hd (Iarray.get receipt.steps 0).created in
          Printf.printf "socket=%s\n%!" socket;
          let pane =
            Snapshot.find_pane
              (get (Client.capture client))
              (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
            |> Option.get
          in
          ignore
            (get
               (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane
                  ~text:"showcase ready"));
          use client initial spawn))

let () =
  let binary = if Array.length Sys.argv = 2 then Sys.argv.(1) else "tmux" in
  with_demo binary (watch_output binary)

nativeDocumentation:
A retained admitted command. A cancelled waiter does not erase its eventual
    success, failure or uncertainty.

declarations.text:
module Operation : sig
  type 'a t

  type cleanup_receipt = {
    cause : Libtmux.Error.t;
    owned_buffers : string list;
    created : Libtmux.Created.t list;
  }
  (** [created] retains IDs reported before a later hook or completion failure.
      It does not prove those resources still exist or authorize retry. When the
      daemon watcher retires an in-flight operation, [cause] retains
      {!Libtmux.Error.Disconnected}. Idle-reader failures also retain their
      library cause instead of becoming an explicit client-close reason. *)

  type 'a state =
    | Queued
    | Not_started
    | Written
    | Acknowledged
    | Finished of ('a, Libtmux.Error.t) result
    | Outcome_unknown of cleanup_receipt

  val id : 'a t -> string

  val inspect : 'a t -> ('a state, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Read without I/O, including after client closure. Owning domain only. *)

  val cancel : 'a t -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove unsent work. A written request remains owned and drained by the
      client. *)

  val await_stage :
    'a t -> [ `Written | `Acknowledged ] -> ('a state, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Wait for the named stage or a terminal state. Acknowledgement does not
      establish completion. Cancelling this observer leaves the operation alone.
  *)
end

nativeDocumentation:
Bounded future-byte observation with Data/Gap/End and local cursors. Polling
    is local; waiting and admission belong to the backend.

declarations.text:
module Subscription : sig
  type t

  val poll : t -> (Libtmux.Output.event option, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Remove a queued event without I/O, on the owning domain. *)

  val next :
    ?timeout:float -> t -> (Libtmux.Output.event option, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Await one event, defaulting to a one-second deadline. [None] follows a
      consumed End. A deadline keeps the subscription active. Eio cancellation
      closes it, releases its lane when unused, and propagates. *)

  val close : t -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** End an active subscription with Cancelled and discard pending data.
      Preserve an already ended subscription's terminal reason. Concurrent calls
      join the same cleanup, including reaping a lane when it becomes unused;
      later calls retain cleanup failures. Borrowed clients and the daemon
      remain alive. {!poll} can still read the terminal event. *)

  val wait_for_bytes :
    ?timeout:float ->
    t ->
    text:string ->
    (Libtmux.Output.cursor, Libtmux.Output.wait_error) result
  (** Consume future observed bytes through a match, with a maximum 64 KiB
      nonempty pattern. Match across Data boundaries and return its end cursor.
      Gaps end matching. This searches neither rendered text nor history. A
      deadline leaves the subscription active; cancellation closes it. *)
end

         ~process_mgr:(Eio.Stdenv.process_mgr env)
         ~mono_clock:(Eio.Stdenv.mono_clock env)
         (Source.endpoint (Libtmux_unix.Client.source blocking)))
  in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Eio.Cancel.protect (fun () -> get (Client.close client)))
    (fun () ->
      let pane =
        Snapshot.find_pane
          (get (Client.capture client))
          (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
        |> Option.get
      in
      let subscription =
        get (Client.subscribe ~capacity_bytes:4096 client pane)
      in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () ->
          Eio.Cancel.protect (fun () -> get (Subscription.close subscription)))
        (fun () ->
          let cursor, () =
            Eio.Fiber.pair
              (fun () ->
                match
                  Subscription.wait_for_bytes ~timeout:0.5 subscription
                    ~text:"changed"
                with
                | Ok cursor -> cursor
                | Error (Output.Failure error) ->
                    failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)
                | Error (Output.Ended reason) ->
                    failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Output.reason_pp reason))
              (fun () ->
                get (Client.send_text client (Pane.target pane) ~text:"changed");
                get (Client.send_keys client (Pane.target pane) [ Key.Enter ]))
          in
          assert (cursor.offset >= 7L);
          print_endline "observed: changed"))

let with_demo binary use =
  let directory = Filename.temp_dir "libtmux-ocaml-showcase-" "" in
  Fun.protect
    ~finally:(fun () ->
      Sys.readdir directory
      |> Array.iter (fun name -> Sys.remove (Filename.concat directory name));
      Unix.rmdir directory)
    (fun () ->
      let socket = Filename.concat directory "server" in
      (* Give this private daemon a lifetime even if startup fails. *)
      let config_file = Filename.concat directory "tmux.conf" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text config_file (fun output ->
          output_string output "set-option -s exit-unattached on\n");
      let wrapper = Filename.concat directory "tmux" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text wrapper (fun output ->
          Printf.fprintf output "#!/bin/sh\nexec %s -f %s \"$@\"\n"
            (Filename.quote binary)
            (Filename.quote config_file));
      Unix.chmod wrapper 0o700;
      let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
      let version =
        Fun.protect
          ~finally:(fun () ->
            if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
              failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
          (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
      in
      if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
        failwith "invalid tmux version";
      let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
      let ready = Filename.concat directory "ready.txt" in
      Out_channel.with_open_text ready (fun output ->
          output_string output "showcase ready\n");
      let spawn =
        Spawn.make (Exec { program = "/bin/cat"; args = [ "-u"; ready; "-" ] })
      in
      let config =
        match
          Config.make ~directory ~session:"showcase"
            [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
      in
      let plan =
        match
          Plan.make
            ~endpoint:(Endpoint.socket_path socket)
            ~version ~observed:None config
        with
        | Ok value -> value
        | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
      in
      let operation = get (Workspace.submit_bootstrap ~binary:wrapper plan) in
      Fun.protect
        ~finally:(fun () -> get (Workspace.close operation))
        (fun () ->
          let receipt = get (Workspace.await operation) in
          if receipt.status <> Execution.Succeeded then
            failwith "workspace setup failed";
          let client = Option.get (Workspace.client operation) in
          let initial = List.hd (Iarray.get receipt.steps 0).created in
          Printf.printf "socket=%s\n%!" socket;
          let pane =
            Snapshot.find_pane
              (get (Client.capture client))
              (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
            |> Option.get
          in
          ignore
            (get
               (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane
                  ~text:"showcase ready"));
          use client initial spawn))

let () =
  let binary = if Array.length Sys.argv = 2 then Sys.argv.(1) else "tmux" in
  with_demo binary (watch_output binary)

Interactive attachment using borrowed application streams. This utility
    addresses the current daemon explicitly and does not reuse captured targets.

declarations.text:
module Terminal : sig
  val attach_current :
    ?cleanup:Cleanup.t ->
    ?binary:string ->
    ?read_only:bool ->
    ?update_environment:bool ->
    ?stdin:_ Eio.Flow.source ->
    ?stdout:_ Eio.Flow.sink ->
    ?stderr:_ Eio.Flow.sink ->
    process_mgr:_ Eio.Process.mgr ->
    Libtmux.Endpoint.t ->
    session:Libtmux.Session.Id.t ->
    (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Run an interactive terminal client until exit, using the application's
      process manager and standard streams unless explicit flows are supplied.
      [stdin] must be backed by a terminal descriptor; a pipe-backed flow is
      rejected by tmux. Select the exact ID on the daemon currently listening at
      [endpoint], without a captured target, binding, retry or daemon startup.

      Environment updates and read-only mode default to false. Clear inherited
      [TMUX] and [TMUX_PANE]. Cancellation propagates after terminating and
      reaping this client; it does not stop the daemon. Cooperative TERM gets
      200 ms of grace before forced termination, while other fibers can run.
      Scheduling and kernel completion can add time. Success proves terminal
      client exit. Diagnostics go to [stderr]; borrowed flows stay open. Supply
      [cleanup] before the call to retain secondary failures after cancellation.
  *)
end

symbols.name: Workspace
nativeDocumentation:
Apply workspace plans through Eio while retaining journals across caller
    cancellation. Handles belong to the creating domain; the application owns
    the scheduler and switch.

declarations.text:
module Workspace : sig
  type t

  val submit :
    Client.t -> Libtmux_workspace.Plan.t -> (t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Allocate a generation-bound handle without I/O. The supplied client is
      borrowed; closing the handle leaves it open. *)

  val submit_bootstrap :
    ?cleanup:Cleanup.t ->
    ?binary:string ->
    ?timeout:float ->
    sw:Eio.Switch.t ->
    process_mgr:_ Eio.Process.mgr ->
    mono_clock:_ Eio.Time.Mono.t ->
    Libtmux_workspace.Plan.t ->
    (t, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Allocate a missing-endpoint execution without I/O. Await starts control
      new-session and binds that same connection. The handle owns its new client
      within [sw]; it never owns the daemon. *)

  val await :
    ?compensate_on_failure:bool ->
    t ->
    (Libtmux_workspace.Execution.receipt, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Apply steps at most once per execution handle. Expected failures return a
      retained journal. On initial application, [compensate_on_failure] defaults
      to [true], attempting removal of proven newly created panes after failure
      or cancellation. Passing [false] skips that compensation. Eio cancellation
      propagates after progress is recorded and at most 500 ms of protected
      compensation. Admitted commands can still complete under client ownership;
      use {!inspect} before manual recovery. *)

  val inspect :
    t -> (Libtmux_workspace.Execution.receipt, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Copy the retained {!type:Libtmux_workspace.Execution.receipt} without I/O,
      on the owning domain, including after execution or client closure. Pending
      steps can settle as the client progresses; earlier receipts keep their own
      step and cleanup arrays. *)

  val client : t -> Client.t option
  (** Borrow the existing or bootstrapped {!Client.t} without I/O for subsequent
      actions or recovery. {!close} releases a client owned by this workspace
      execution handle. *)

  val close : t -> (unit, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Release an owned client through {!Client.close}. Active await returns
      Busy. Closing is idempotent; completed journals remain readable. *)
end

  val decode :
    'a Libtmux.Model.t ->
    Yojson.Safe.t ->
    ('a Libtmux.Expr.t, Decode_error.t) result
  (** Validate the supplied tree, including duplicate properties, before typed
      construction. Only the shared scalar pane registry and Boolean composition
      are accepted. Java regex, relationships and native extension fields return
      [Unsupported]. Numbers must fit signed 32-bit integers. *)

  val of_string :
    'a Libtmux.Model.t -> string -> ('a Libtmux.Expr.t, Decode_error.t) result
  (** Enforce 64 KiB and 32 JSON nesting levels before parsing; require valid
      UTF-8 JSON. Expressions have at most 1,024 nodes and membership lists at
      most 256 values. Errors include a JSON pointer, never the whole input. *)

    'a Libtmux.Model.t ->

    (Yojson.Safe.t, Decode_error.t) result

  val to_string :
    'a Libtmux.Model.t -> 'a Libtmux.Expr.t -> (string, Decode_error.t) result
  (** Apply the same bounds and subset when encoding. Text with invalid UTF-8
      has no representation in this schema. These functions perform no I/O. *)
end

symbols.name: Libtmux_unix
nativeDocumentation:
Blocking Linux tmux clients with explicit scoped cancellation.

    Client methods perform I/O unless documented otherwise. Captured
    {!Libtmux.Snapshot} observations and retained {!Operation.inspect} remain
    local. Clients belong to the connecting domain. Closure releases their owned
    resources; tmux applies its configured daemon lifetime.

    See {!Client} for acquisition and commands, {!Operation} for cancellation
    outcomes, and {!Subscription} for bounded future output. The

See {!Client} for acquisition and commands, {!Operation} for cancellation outcomes, and {!Subscription} for bounded future output. The [control guide](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ocaml/blob/master/docs/control.md) explains binding, completion and recovery.

module Cancellation : sig
  type t

  exception Cancelled

  val with_ : (t -> 'a) -> 'a
  (** Own a cancellation token for the callback's lifetime. Leaving the scope
      cancels outstanding waiters and releases its descriptors after they
      finish. An escaped token is cancelled and cannot be reused. *)

  val cancel : t -> unit
  (** Wake waiters. Safe from another domain or systhread, but not from a signal
      handler. Repeated calls and calls after scope exit have no effect. *)
end

declarations.text:
module Cleanup : sig
  type t = Cleanup.t

  type phase = Cleanup.phase =
    | Close_pipe
    | Open_pidfd
    | Close_pidfd
    | Terminate
    | Grace
    | Kill
    | Reap
    | Unreaped_child
    | Cancel_workers
    | Release_hook
    | Notify_waiters

  type issue = Cleanup.issue = {
    phase : phase;
    error : Libtmux.Error.t option;
    exception_ : exn;
    backtrace : Printexc.raw_backtrace;
  }
  (** One failed cleanup action. [error] retains a typed library cause when
      available; [exception_] and [backtrace] retain the original exception.
      [Unreaped_child] means exit was not established after a failed signal. It
      does not release ownership or authorize signalling a reused PID. *)

  type snapshot = Cleanup.snapshot = { issues : issue Iarray.t; omitted : int }
  (** Issues in occurrence order, with a count of additional omitted issues. A
      report retains at most 64 entries. This bounds entry count, not heap
      retention: exception payloads and backtraces may retain other values.
      These diagnostics are not immutable graph observations. *)

  val create : unit -> t
  (** Create an empty report without I/O. Supply it before {!Client.connect},
      {!Workspace.submit_bootstrap} or {!Terminal.attach_current} to retain
      cleanup evidence even when setup fails or cancellation raises. *)

  val inspect : t -> (snapshot, Libtmux.Error.t) result
  (** Copy the current diagnostics without I/O. Returns
      {!Libtmux.Error.Wrong_domain} outside the creating domain. *)
end
